facts.statement: The holotype fossil was discovered in 1994 by Zhou Zhonghe in the Boluochi quarry within the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype IVPP 10916 was in 1994 found in the Boluochi quarry by Zhou Zhonghe in a layer of the Jiufotang Formation dating from the late Aptian.

facts.statement: The bones of the holotype have been preserved only as impressions.
facts.quote: The bones have only been preserved as impressions.

facts.statement: Eocathayornis is a genus of enantiornithean birds considered more basal or primitive than related genera like Sinornis and Cathayornis.
facts.quote: Eocathayornis is a genus of enantiornithean birds that was probably more basal or "primitive" than related genera Sinornis and Cathayornis.

facts.statement: These birds lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now the People's Republic of China.
facts.quote: These birds lived during the Early Cretaceous in today's People's Republic of China.

facts.statement: Zhou placed Eocathayornis in the family Cathayornithidae in 2002.
facts.quote: Zhou in 2002 placed Eocathayornis in the Cathayornithidae.

facts.statement: Recent studies show the phylogenetic position of Eocathayornis is labile, varying between affiliations with Bohaiornithidae, basal positions near Pengornithidae, or advanced positions depending on included taxa.
facts.quote: In all three of these more recent studies, the position of Eocathayornis, Sulcavis (and probably Shenqiornis), and Eoenantiornis was notably labile, varying between a close affiliation with Bohaiornithidae and a more basal (and possibly close to Pengornithidae) or advanced position, depending on whether taxa such as Concornis, Navaornis, Neobohaiornis, or one or both of Fortunguavis and Vescornis, were included.

facts.statement: A 2024 analysis supported a clade linking Cathayornis and Eocathayornis, though this was considered less comprehensive than a 2026 study.
facts.quote: While the 2024 description of Navaornis did support a Cathayornis-Eocathayornis clade, this analysis was a less-comprehensive version of the 2026 Gorgonavis study.

facts.statement: Eocathayornis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
Eocathayornis is an extinct avialan belonging to the Enantiornithes clade that inhabited the Early Cretaceous in present-day China.
facts.quote: Eocathayornis es un género extinto de avialano perteneciente al clado Enantiornithes que habitó en el Cretácico inferior en lo que hoy es China.

facts.statement: The time range for Eocathayornis is from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
